sourceDocument: Existing user-approved FND-7 scope and decisions, refreshed against official OBS/Chromium documentation on 2026-10-06.

functional.description: Let the streamer create, edit, and delete independent overlay widgets, each bound to one supported data field or fixed custom text, and generate one OBS browser-source link per widget.
functional.rationale: The streamer asked for independent links so each value can be positioned and styled separately in OBS.
acceptance: AC-1: Given an authenticated streamer, when they create or edit a widget, then they choose one atomic supported field or fixed text and its optional queue scope without changing business state.

AC-12: Given an existing widget, when the authenticated streamer deletes it, then widget deletion and capability invalidation commit atomically; after success, no read using the prior token can return data and business state is unchanged.

functional.description: Offer one atomic data widget for current Genshin account label, selected queue name, selected queue open/closed state, selected queue waiting count, called viewer display name, called viewer original waiting position at call time, or in-service viewer display name; also support fixed text. Queue-scoped widgets select exactly one queue. When multiple viewers are in called state, called-viewer fields resolve to the earliest outstanding call ordered by calledAt then createdAt.
functional.rationale: The streamer selected all proposed operational data for the first release; each widget remains limited to its selected field and queue.
acceptance: AC-1: Given a new widget, when the streamer selects a source, then the catalog offers these atomic sources: current Genshin account label; selected queue name; selected queue state; selected queue waiting count; called viewer display name; called viewer original waiting position at the moment of call, read from its audited transition snapshot rather than the now-null waiting position; in-service viewer display name; or fixed text. When multiple viewers are called, resolve called-viewer fields to the earliest outstanding call ordered by calledAt then createdAt. No combined data fields are implicit.
AC-5: Given a valid widget capability, when its projection is read, then only that selected field and required queue scope are returned; UID and unrelated records are absent.

functional.description: Let the streamer configure text color, optional background color and opacity, allowlisted local font stack, size, weight, alignment, none/outline/shadow effect, widget dimensions, margins, overflow, and fallback text; enforce bounded values and a 240 Unicode-code-point limit on fixed/fallback text.
functional.rationale: The streamer selected complete per-element styling and configurable text when a dynamic value is absent.
acceptance: AC-3: Given a widget editor, when the streamer changes an allowed style field, then preview and OBS use it and both browser/API reject unsupported or malformed values. Colors use #RRGGBB; font size is integer 8–128px; weight is one of 300,400,500,600,700,800,900; opacity is 0–100%; width is auto or 1–3840px; height is auto or 1–2160px; margins are 0–256px; overflow is wrap/clip/ellipsis. Outline thickness is 1–8px; shadow blur is 0–32px with each offset −32 to 32px.
AC-10: Given fixed or fallback text, when it exceeds 240 Unicode code points, then browser and API reject it using the same counting rule; all text is rendered inertly.

functional.description: Preview a widget; issue and show its OBS URL exactly once when a widget is created or its capability is regenerated; allow copying that newly issued link, revocation, and regeneration without changing widget source/style. Never provide an endpoint that retrieves an already issued raw secret.
functional.rationale: The link is a read-only capability and the user explicitly selected revocation and regeneration.
acceptance: AC-2: Given widget creation or capability regeneration through the authenticated panel, when that mutation succeeds, then the response returns the secret-bearing local URL exactly once for immediate display/copy; the raw token is never persisted, logged, cached, placed in HTTP path/query, or retrievable through later reads. The OBS read-only projection endpoint never returns the capability secret.
AC-6: Given an active widget link, when the streamer revokes or regenerates it, then the prior capability fails; widget source/style remain unchanged, and regeneration issues a new one-time URL.

functional.description: Refresh dynamic widget data so changes in local account, queue, and service state appear in OBS within two seconds; show configured fallback when the source is empty; during transient network/server failure retain the last value with a visible stale marker until recovery.
functional.rationale: The user selected a two-second update target, configured text for empty values, and the last value with an explicit stale marker during transient failure.
acceptance: AC-7: Given a healthy local app and eight concurrently open widgets using mixed dynamic fields, when a source-state change is committed, then the corresponding widget renders it within two seconds from commit to rendered DOM. Run ten consecutive changes; every measurement must pass, with the environment recorded.

AC-11: Given an empty field, when a successful projection returns no value, then show configured fallback. Given transport/server failure after a value, retain it with a visible stale marker and retry; if initial fetch fails before any value, show neutral unavailable state. Given 401/403 or deleted widget, clear the value and show neutral unavailable state.

functional.description: Expose an OBS browser-source page and a read-only data endpoint that use the same application/domain projections as the panel, chat, and workers.
functional.rationale: A second source of business state would make the overlay disagree with the bot and could bypass UID visibility rules.
acceptance: AC-13: Given an OBS read or operator-panel mutation, when a route handles it, then it calls shared application/domain projections and does not query business entities directly or duplicate transition rules.
AC-8: Given an OBS capability, when a request is made, then it cannot invoke a mutation route.

functional.description: Keep each overlay link local to the same computer as the bot and OBS; its unguessable, revocable capability can read only its widget and cannot call administrative mutations.
functional.rationale: The user selected same-computer operation; the existing product is local and has no hosted backend.
acceptance: AC-14: Given an OBS capability, when used on the same computer, then it grants read-only access to exactly one widget and no session/admin privileges.

AC-15: Given a revoked, replaced, or deleted-widget capability, when used again, then no widget data is returned and browser renderer clears previously displayed content; deletion commits atomically with capability invalidation.

functional.description: Document setup and use of overlay links in English and pt-BR, including the OBS browser-source URL, viewport sizing, transparency, refresh behavior, and token revocation.
functional.rationale: Streamers need actionable setup guidance for a new OBS integration.
acceptance: AC-9: Given a streamer setting up OBS, when they follow either English or pt-BR guide, then it explains browser source, local URL, dimensions, transparency, refresh behavior, preview, and revoke/regenerate steps.

functional.description: Keep OBS Browser Source limited to rendering the local overlay: do not use OBS-specific JavaScript bindings, scene/control APIs, or OBS data; guide the streamer to set Browser Source Page Permissions to None.
functional.rationale: The overlay needs only same-origin widget data. Official OBS documentation says the Browser Source exposes configurable page permissions, whose default permits reading OBS status.
acceptance: AC-16: Given the streamer adds a widget in OBS, when they configure the Browser Source, then the guide instructs Page Permissions = None; the overlay does not read window.obsstudio or call OBS-specific APIs.

nonFunctional.description: On the local installation, a committed account, queue, call, or service-state change is rendered by the overlay within 2 seconds under normal operation.

Capability is read-only and widget-scoped; raw secret is disclosed only once in the create/regenerate response, never later re-read or persisted; UIDs, Twitch credentials, sessions and unrelated data are excluded.
The OBS page has a transparent background, no scrollbars at its configured viewport, and uses only local application assets and allowlisted system font stacks.

Empty values show configured fallback; transient fetch failures retain the last value only with a visible stale marker and automatically retry; invalid/revoked capability clears the value on rejection.
Widget output is rendered as text with a strict style schema; user input cannot inject HTML, JavaScript, arbitrary CSS, or remote asset URLs.
Widget controls are labeled, keyboard-operable, show focus, and provide a readability preview before link copying.
For every OS/OBS version claimed as supported, the CEF Browser Source loads the local HTTPS overlay using the trusted application certificate without a certificate bypass or insecure HTTP fallback.

constraints.description: The feature is a same-computer OBS integration for the existing single-broadcaster local application; it must not add public hosting, a cloud backend, telemetry, LAN access, or a second runtime service.
Use the existing apps/web, apps/api, Fastify, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and vanilla JavaScript layout; add no dependency unless research and a failing test demonstrate it is needed.
All data reads go through existing application/domain services and safe projections; do not duplicate queue, account, privacy, or transition rules in the overlay route.

One secret per widget; do not put it in HTTP request paths/queries or persist raw value. Creation/regeneration returns the newly issued URL exactly once; subsequent reads cannot recover it. Allow immediate revocation.
The user's explicit feature request supersedes the earlier FND-0 MVP non-goal for this separately tracked post-MVP story; the original MVP baseline remains historically accurate.
The operator panel remains the control surface selected in the approved product planning; do not add a separate product CLI for overlay management.

FND-5 and FND-6 must be fully complete and their field projections and protected panel foundations verified before any FND-7 implementation begins; no reduced field subset is accepted as a workaround.

Keep Browser Source on the app’s local HTTPS origin. Never disable certificate validation or fall back to HTTP to work around CEF trust-store differences; document only trust steps verified on the tested OS/OBS version.

assumptions.description: OBS Studio's official Browser Source is installed and can load the local application URL on the same computer.
The currently supported local bot and its PostgreSQL service are running while the OBS source is active; a transient outage keeps the last rendered value with a stale marker until recovery.
A single widget has one selected data field or fixed text, one optional queue scope, one style configuration, and one independently revocable link; duplicate widgets are allowed.
Fonts are selected from safe generic/local system font stacks; downloading or embedding third-party fonts is not required.
The OBS CEF runtime can trust the local HTTPS certificate after platform-appropriate installation; its trust behavior may differ from the desktop browser and must be checked natively.

domainModel.description: A streamer-managed, read-only display element containing one source field or fixed text, optional queue scope, fallback text, and validated style settings.
relationships: References a queue when its source field is queue-scoped.
References a single capability secret by hash.

domainModel.description: An unguessable secret granting read access to exactly one widget until revoked or regenerated.
relationships: Belongs to one OverlayWidget; cannot access administrative or other widget data.

domainModel.description: An allowlisted projection of current account, queue, waiting count, called viewer/its audited prior waiting position, or in-service viewer state.
relationships: Reads source state through application/domain projections.

interactions.description: Streamer opens Overlay in the local panel, selects exactly one atomic source field or fixed text, selects a queue for queue-scoped fields, configures style/fallback, previews, saves, receives a one-time URL, copies it, and adds it as an OBS Browser Source.
OBS loads the local widget page; the page reads its fragment capability into memory, fetches only its widget projection, and refreshes it; a changed value appears within two seconds.

Streamer confirms revoke, regenerate, or delete in the panel; revocation/deletion invalidates the prior capability and returns no replacement URL. Regeneration invalidates the prior capability and shows the new URL once for copying.
states: one-time replacement URL only after regeneration

edgeCases.scenario: A source field has no current value, such as no viewer being called.
edgeCases.handling: Render the widget's configured fallback text; do not retain the last dynamic value.

edgeCases.scenario: The local API or database is temporarily unavailable after the page loads.
edgeCases.handling: Keep the last value visible with an explicit stale marker, retry automatically, and replace it on recovery; if there is no prior value, show a neutral unavailable state.

edgeCases.scenario: The capability is missing, invalid, revoked, or belongs to another widget.
edgeCases.handling: Return no private widget data; clear any previously displayed value on the 401/403 response, show a neutral unavailable state, and allow the streamer to generate a replacement from the protected panel.

edgeCases.scenario: Streamer enters markup, script, invalid colors, unsupported font values, or out-of-range style values.
edgeCases.handling: Validate at the server boundary, reject invalid configuration, and render accepted text only as text with allowlisted style properties.

edgeCases.scenario: A selected queue is archived/deleted or its widget field is no longer available.
edgeCases.handling: Do not read another queue; show fallback and identify the configuration as needing repair in the panel.

edgeCases.scenario: OBS CEF does not trust the local application CA even though the desktop browser does.
edgeCases.handling: Do not bypass TLS or switch the overlay to HTTP. Record the exact OS/OBS/CEF environment, verify the supported trust-store path, and do not claim that environment as supported until the Browser Source loads the local HTTPS page normally.

edgeCases.scenario: The Browser Source has unnecessary OBS page privileges enabled.
edgeCases.handling: The guide asks the operator to set Page Permissions to None. The overlay remains functional without OBS bindings and never reads OBS state or invokes OBS control APIs.

terminology.definition: One independently configured OBS display element and its read-only browser-source link.
A local URL whose private secret grants read-only access to exactly one overlay widget until revoked.
Streamer-configured text shown when a dynamic source field has no current value; transient transport errors instead show the last value with a stale marker.

openQuestions.question: Which default style preset, color palette, and exact allowlisted system font names best fit the existing panel's visual guidance? Resolve in the UX refinement before UI implementation.
The custom text limit is 240 Unicode code points; enforce the same counting rule in browser and API.
Which safe default style, font labels, preview and stale/unavailable presentations best fit the panel? Resolve in UX refinement.

Which OBS/OS versions have a trusted CEF path for the app’s HTTPS local certificate, and what trust-store steps work without bypassing validation? Verify with native Browser Source before claiming compatibility.
